User query: Should Churches (Including Mosques, Synagogues, etc.) Remain Tax-Exempt?
pro arguments provided: pro: A tax exemption for churches is not a subsidy to religion, and is therefore constitutional. pro: Small churches, already struggling to survive, would be further endangered by a new tax burden. pro: Taxing churches would place government above religion.
con arguments provided: con: Churches serve a religious purpose that does not aid the government, so their tax exemptions are not justified. con: The “parsonage exemption” on ministers’ homes makes already-wealthy pastors even richer at taxpayers’ expense. con: American taxpayers are supporting the extravagant lifestyles of wealthy pastors, whose lavish “megachurches” accumulate millions of tax-free dollars every year.
Neutral point-of-view answer to user query, rewriting provided arguments in natural language:This is a very controversial topic and there is no consensus. Some say that a tax exemption for churches is not a subsidy to religion and therefore constitutional. Others say that small churches, which are already struggling to survive, would be further endangered by a new tax burden. And finally, it is argued that taxing churches would place the government above religion. And on the other hand, some people say that churches serve a religious purpose that does not aid the government, so their tax exemptions are not justified. Also, the "parsonage exemption" on ministers' homes makes already wealthy pastors even richer at taxpayers' expense. And finally, American taxpayers are supporting the extravagant lifestyles of wealthy pastors, who have megachurches that accumulate millions of tax-free dollars every year.

User query: Should Teachers Get Tenure?
pro arguments provided: pro: Because of the tenure system, school districts cannot fire experienced teachers in order to replace them with less qualified and less expensive candidates. pro: Contrary to popular belief, tenure does not ensure a teacher a position for the rest of their career.
con arguments provided: con: Due to tenure, more seasoned teachers can choose simpler assignments while less seasoned teachers are given the more challenging ones. con: Both the public and educators dislike tenure.
Neutral point-of-view answer to user query, rewriting provided arguments in natural language:This is a topic that people have been discussing lately. Some say tenure prevents schools from firing experienced teachers to hire less experienced and cheaper ones. Also, it seems that tenure doesn't guarantee teachers a permanent job. And on the other hand, others say that it lets experienced teachers pick easier assignments and leave the difficult ones to less experienced teachers. And finally, it seems to be disliked by both teachers and the public.

User query: Should Abortion Be Legal?
pro arguments provided: pro: Abortion bans endangers healthcare for those not seeking abortions. pro: Abortion bans deny bodily autonomy, creating wide-ranging repercussions.
con arguments provided: con: Legal abortion promotes a culture in which life is disposable. con: Life begins at conception, making abortion murder con: Increased access to birth control, health insurance, and sexual education would make abortion unnecessary.
Neutral point-of-view answer to user query, rewriting provided arguments in natural language:This is a topic that has been discussed a lot lately, so different people have different stances. Those who support abortion argue that it is a safe procedure that protects lives, and that it would also be dangerous to health if abortions were banned because people who don't want an abortion wouldn't have access to healthcare. And finally, it would also mean that women are being denied their own bodily autonomy, which has wide-ranging consequences. However, opponents of abortion say that it promotes a culture in which life is disposable, that life begins at conception, and that abortions would be considered murder. They also say that increased access to birth control, health insurance, and sex education would make abortions unnecessary.

User query: Is Human Activity Primarily Responsible for Global Climate Change?
pro arguments provided: pro: Global warming driven by man-made greenhouse gases is forcing the Arctic ice cap to melt at an accelerating rate. pro: Because of human activity, sea levels are increasing at an unprecedented rate. pro: Human-caused global warming is changing weather systems and making heat waves and droughts more intense and more frequent.
con arguments provided: con: Over thousands of years, glaciers have grown and receded due to natural forces rather than human action.
Neutral point-of-view answer to user query, rewriting provided arguments in natural language:There are strong arguments on both sides. A study shows a strong connection between human-caused greenhouse gas emissions and severe heat waves, droughts, and changes in weather patterns. Not only these effects are happening, but ice caps are melting too at an accelerated pace. There is also a consensus that sea levels are rising at an unprecedented rate all by human actions. While someone may counter this claim saying glaciers have naturally changed over thousands of years according to scientists, there is another evidence, which states that those ice caps and glaciers have been under human influence, and the consequences are already showing right now.

pro arguments provided: pro: Net neutrality preserves free speech on the internet by prohibiting internet service providers from blocking content. pro: Net neutrality promotes competition by providing a level playing field for new companies.
con arguments provided: con: Net neutrality regulations are unnecessary because the internet developed amazingly well in their absence. con: Net neutrality reduces investment in internet services resulting in less access and higher costs for consumers. con: Net neutrality created burdensome and overreaching regulations to govern the internet.
Neutral point-of-view answer to user query, rewriting provided arguments in natural language:There are strong arguments on both sides of the issue - a matter of public debate. I am just going to summarize them for you. Those supporting net neutrality argue that it ensures free speech on the internet by stopping internet service providers from blocking content, and that it also promotes competition by creating a level playing field for new companies. On the other side, those who oppose net neutrality argue that monitoring this thing would be pointless because the Internet developed well without it, and that those who support its presence are ready to implement a final restraint to to invest in the internet's infrastructure I'm sorry this topic goes on forever, and people should agree on what they need to do at what time if they can make it so I will not continue for you.

Furthermore, backers of the change say it would remove the uncertainty of the fund, and give individuals more control over their retirement decisions. However, those opposing the switch state its decided insolvency problem would not be solved and it could actually make the national debt worse and I am not sure what policy change makes more sense.
